claims.statement: e2b-client is a publishable async Rust client for the standard E2B API, usable against hosted E2B and E2B-compatible servers.
The client covers the official SDK's Sandbox/SandboxApi lifecycle surface against hosted E2B.
The client covers the official SDK's Commands (process) surface against hosted E2B.
The client covers the official SDK's Filesystem surface against hosted E2B.
Every wire fact in docs/protocol-notes.md is implemented as documented.
The crate meets the bar for publishing on crates.io: live-verified, stable reviewed API, documented, released.
Client::create_sandbox with a template returns a running Sandbox whose sandbox_id, template_id and envd_version are populated.
CreateSandboxParams metadata entries are visible in get_sandbox_info of the created sandbox.
CreateSandboxParams env vars are present in the environment of commands run in the created sandbox.
CreateSandboxParams timeout sets the sandbox end_at to about started_at plus the timeout.
CreateSandboxParams auto_pause(true) makes the sandbox pause, not die, when its timeout expires.
CreateSandboxParams allow_internet_access(false) blocks outbound internet access from the sandbox.
Client::connect_sandbox on a running sandbox returns a Sandbox that can run commands.
Client::connect_sandbox resumes a paused sandbox with its filesystem state preserved.
Client::connect_sandbox on an unknown sandbox id returns Error::SandboxNotFound.
Client::get_sandbox_info returns the sandbox's state, template_id, metadata, started_at and end_at.
Client::get_sandbox_info on an unknown sandbox id returns Error::SandboxNotFound.
Client::list_sandboxes filtered by metadata returns exactly the sandboxes carrying that metadata.
Client::list_sandboxes filtered by state returns only sandboxes in that state.
Client::list_sandboxes with limit and next_token pages through all matching sandboxes with no duplicates or omissions.
Client::kill_sandbox on a running sandbox returns true and the sandbox is then not found.
Client::kill_sandbox on an unknown sandbox id returns false, not an error.
Client::pause_sandbox on a running sandbox returns true and the sandbox state becomes Paused.
Client::pause_sandbox on an already paused sandbox returns false, not an error.
Client::set_sandbox_timeout moves the sandbox end_at to about now plus the timeout.
Client::refresh_sandbox with a duration extends the sandbox end_at.
Sandbox::is_running returns true for a running sandbox and false after it is killed.
Sandbox::get_host(port) returns the host name that reaches a service listening on that port inside the sandbox.
The client can read sandbox CPU, memory and disk metrics as the SDK's get_metrics does.
The client can snapshot a sandbox and create (fork) sandboxes from a snapshot as the SDK does.
The client can update a running sandbox's network settings as the SDK does.
create_sandbox can send every create field SDK 2.61 sends (secure, network, lifecycle, mcp) beyond the v0.1 set.
Commands::run returns the command's full stdout, stderr and exit code, and a non-zero exit is not an Err.
Commands::start returns a handle whose next_event yields Stdout and Stderr chunks as they are produced, then Exit.
Commands::run delivers large output (at least 1 MiB) complete and in order.
CommandOptions env entries are set in the command's environment.
CommandOptions cwd sets the command's working directory.
CommandOptions user runs the command as that user.
CommandOptions timeout ends the wait on a command that outlives it with Error::Timeout or a deadline_exceeded Rpc error.
Commands::connect(pid) attaches to a running command and receives its later output and exit code.
Commands::list includes a running background command with its pid and command line.
Commands::send_stdin delivers bytes to the stdin of a command started with stdin(true).
Commands::close_stdin delivers EOF so a command reading stdin to the end exits.
Commands::send_signal(Sigterm) terminates a running command.
Commands::kill returns true for a running pid and false for an unknown pid.
The client can stream stdin to a command with envd's StreamInput RPC.
The client can start a PTY session and receive its output, as the SDK's pty.create does.
The client can resize a PTY session.
The client can send input to a PTY session.
Filesystem::write then Filesystem::read round-trips arbitrary binary bytes unchanged.
Filesystem::read_to_string returns a UTF-8 file's text.
Filesystem::write returns a WriteInfo with the written path and FileType::File.
Filesystem::read of a missing file returns an error for which is_not_found() is true.
Filesystem::list with depth 1 returns a directory's direct entries with correct file types.
Filesystem::list with depth 2 also returns entries of subdirectories.
Filesystem::get_info returns an entry's size, file type, permissions and owner.
Filesystem::exists is true for an existing path and false for a missing one.
Filesystem::make_dir returns true when it creates a directory and false when it already exists.
Filesystem::rename moves an entry and returns its info at the new path.
Filesystem::remove deletes a file or directory so that exists is then false.
Filesystem operations given a user act as that user (a file written as root is owned by root).
The client can write several files in one request, as the SDK's write_files does.
The client can watch a directory and receive filesystem events, as the SDK's watch_dir does.
The client can produce a signed upload URL for a sandbox path, as the SDK's upload_url does.
The client can produce a signed download URL for a sandbox path, as the SDK's download_url does.
The client can upload a file larger than memory by streaming it, with octet-stream or gzip encoding as the SDK supports.
ConnectionConfig reads the domain from E2B_DOMAIN and defaults it to e2b.app.
ConnectionConfig reads the API key from E2B_API_KEY.
ConnectionConfig reads the API URL from E2B_API_URL and otherwise uses https://api.<domain>.
ConnectionConfig reads an envd URL override from E2B_SANDBOX_URL.
Each ConnectionConfig setting resolves as explicit value, then env var, then default, with an empty value counted as unset.
The default request timeout is 60 seconds.
REST requests carry the API key in the X-API-KEY header.
envd RPCs go to the E2B_SANDBOX_URL override, else https://sandbox.<domain> for hosted E2B domains, else https://49983-<sandbox_id>.<domain>.
envd file API requests go to the override, else always https://49983-<sandbox_id>.<domain>.
envd addressing uses the domain returned by the API for the sandbox, else the configured domain.
Every envd request carries E2b-Sandbox-Id: <id> and E2b-Sandbox-Port: 49983.
envd requests carry X-Access-Token when the API returned an envd access token, and never the API key.
envd RPCs select the acting user with Authorization: Basic base64("<user>:"), sending none without a user except defaulting to user for envd older than 0.4.0.
The envd file API selects the acting user with the username query parameter, with the same defaulting as RPCs.
Process streams carry Keepalive-Ping-Interval: 50.
An unparseable or debug envd version is treated as 99.99.99.
create_sandbox sends POST /v2/sandboxes and accepts 201 with a Sandbox body.
The create body uses templateID, timeout, autoPause, metadata, envVars and allow_internet_access, omitting unset fields.
The created-sandbox response is parsed from templateID, sandboxID, clientID, envdVersion and the optional envdAccessToken, trafficAccessToken and domain.
connect_sandbox sends POST /v2/sandboxes/{id}/connect with body {timeout?} and accepts 200 or 201.
When v2 connect answers 404, connect_sandbox retries POST /sandboxes/{id}/connect with body {timeout} before reporting not found.
get_sandbox_info sends GET /sandboxes/{id} and parses SandboxDetail, mapping 404 to SandboxNotFound.
SandboxState parses running and paused.
list_sandboxes sends GET /v2/sandboxes with metadata, state, limit and nextToken query parameters.
list_sandboxes reads the next page token from the x-next-token response header.
list_sandboxes sends multiple states comma-joined in one state parameter.
list_sandboxes encodes the metadata filter by encodeURIComponent-ing each key and value and form-encoding them into one string.
kill_sandbox sends DELETE /sandboxes/{id}, treats 204 as true and 404 as false.
pause_sandbox sends POST /sandboxes/{id}/pause with body {}, treats 204 as true, 409 as false and 404 as SandboxNotFound.
set_sandbox_timeout sends POST /sandboxes/{id}/timeout with body {timeout} in seconds, mapping 404 to SandboxNotFound.
refresh_sandbox sends POST /sandboxes/{id}/refreshes with body {duration?} in seconds and accepts 204.
A non-2xx REST answer becomes Error::Api carrying the status and the body's message field.
envd RPCs are sent as POST <base>/<package.Service>/<Method> using the Connect JSON codec, uncompressed.
Unary RPCs use Content-Type application/json and streaming RPCs application/connect+json, both with Connect-Protocol-Version: 1.
RPC deadlines are sent in Connect-Timeout-Ms as whole milliseconds, at least 1.
Streaming RPC messages are framed as a 1-byte flag plus a 4-byte big-endian length plus the payload, including when split across network reads.
An end-of-stream envelope (flag 0x02) ends the stream, and its error object becomes Error::Rpc.
A Connect error body's snake_case code string maps to the matching ConnectCode, with its message kept.
A non-Connect error body maps to a ConnectCode by HTTP status, and an integer JSON code is taken as the status.
Commands are started as /bin/bash -l -c <cmd> with envs, cwd and stdin defaulting to false.
Opening a process stream requires the first event to be start within the request timeout, and takes the pid from it.
A process stream that ends without an end event is an error.
close_stdin is refused with an error for envd versions older than 0.5.2.

File reads send GET /files?path=

[&username=] and return the body bytes.

File writes send POST /files?path=

as multipart/form-data field file named by the path and parse the JSON array of {name, type, path}.
envd file API errors become Error::Envd with the status and the body's message.
Filesystem::list rejects depth 0 with Error::InvalidArgument without a request.
EntryInfo parses the proto3 JSON EntryInfo, including int64 size as a string and FileType enum names.
Sandbox::is_running sends GET /health and treats 502 as not running.
Process event JSON (start, data stdout/stderr base64 bytes, end with exit_code and error, keepalive) parses into CommandEvent values.
Every v0.1 S1-S3 claim is supported by a live run against hosted E2B.
Every v0.1 S1-S3 claim has been run live against sandbawks, with each failure either fixed in the crate or filed against gfd/sandbawks.
Public structs and enums that may gain fields or variants are #[non_exhaustive].
Every public item has a rustdoc comment, enforced by the missing_docs lint, and public functions with non-trivial use have examples.
The crate states its semver policy and pins a minimum supported Rust version (rust-version) that CI checks.
No API key or envd access token appears in the Debug output of Client, ConnectionConfig or Sandbox.
A CI job runs the live suite against hosted E2B using repository secrets on a manual or nightly trigger.
Cargo.toml allows publishing and cargo publish --dry-run succeeds.
The crate contains no sandbawks-specific endpoints or behaviour beyond the standard E2B API.
The crate is licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 and vendors no third-party material that needs a NOTICE.
